title: Assembling fiber colimit cones on a Grothendieck collage
statement: Use quasicategories, nerves, coherent diagrams, mapping spaces and colimits as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $I$ be a small ordinary category and $U:I\to\mathrm{Cat}$ a strict functor to small ordinary categories. Define $K=\int_I U$: its objects are $(i,x)$ with $x\in U(i)$, and a morphism $(i,x)\to(j,y)$ is $(f,\alpha)$ with $f:i\to j$ and $\alpha:U(f)(x)\to y$, composed by $(g,\beta)(f,\alpha)=(gf,\beta\,U(g)(\alpha))$. Write $p:K\to I$ for projection. Define the collage $P$ with disjoint full subcategories $K$ and $I$, with $\operatorname{Hom}_P(k,i)=\operatorname{Hom}_I(p(k),i)$ and $\operatorname{Hom}_P(i,k)=\varnothing$; mixed composition uses $p$ and composition in $I$. Let $Q:N(K)\to\mathcal E$ be a coherent diagram in a quasicategory. Suppose $Q_i=Q|_{N(U(i))}$ has a colimit for every $i\in I$. Then there exists $\overline Q:N(P)\to\mathcal E$ restricting to $Q$, such that the cocone on $Q_i$ with apex $\overline Q(i)$ induced by the arrows $(i,x)\to i$ labeled $1_i$ is colimiting, for every $i$. Empty fibers require initial objects. No preservation of colimits by $U(f)$ or by $Q$ is assumed.

source.place: Kerodon Proposition 7.3.4.7 (02ZW), with target base the point, together with Proposition 7.3.4.3 (02ZP). Apply to the nerve of the Grothendieck projection; its chosen cocartesian lifts are (f,identity), and its relative join with N(I) is the nerve of the displayed collage. Both pages read online; not archived in literature/. These are Kerodon identifiers, not Stacks tags.

proof.text: Choose a colimiting coherent cocone for each $Q_i$. We first realize each as an actual diagram on $N(U(i)^{\triangleright})$ extending exactly $Q_i$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-join-cone-calculus] to $N(U(i))^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}$, then take opposites. Reversing the simplex order interchanges left and right join cones and constant-to-diagram with diagram-to-constant transformations; inner horns remain inner horns, so the opposite is a quasicategory. The comparison in that node is an equivalence even after fixing the boundary diagram and apex. Thus it supplies a right-join cone whose coherent cocone is equivalent, with boundary and apex fixed, to the chosen one. The dual cocone category is a quasicategory by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. The comparison preserves its initial objects: if two cocones are equivalent, composition with an equivalence and its inverse gives mutually inverse maps of their outgoing mapping spaces, with the inverse homotopies furnished by the two equivalence identities. Thus contractibility of every outgoing mapping space, and hence the colimiting property, is preserved. Denote the resulting actual diagram by $c_i:N(U(i)^{\triangleright})\to\mathcal E$. This also applies to an empty fiber: its cone is a single vertex representing the assumed initial object.

source.place: Lemma 7.3.4.6, choose the fiber cones; agent expansion matching the project coherent-comma convention

proof.text: Extend $p$ to $\pi:P\to I$ by the identity on the second copy of $I$. The mixed composition rule makes this a functor. Its strict fiber at $i$ consists of $U(i)$ and the second-copy vertex $i$, with one arrow from every $x\in U(i)$ to that vertex; thus it is exactly $U(i)^{\triangleright}$. Put $A=N(K)$ and $S_m=A\cup(N\pi)^{-1}(\operatorname{sk}_m N(I))$, where the skeleton consists of simplices generated from nondegenerate simplices of dimension at most $m$. The subsets over different vertices have disjoint new parts and intersect $A$ in precisely their bases $N(U(i))$. Consequently $Q$ and all $c_i$ glue degree by degree to a simplicial map $F_0:S_0\to\mathcal E$. Their values agree on each intersection because each $c_i$ extends exactly $Q_i$.

source.place: Lemma 7.3.4.6, amalgamation of the given diagram and the chosen fiber cocones

proof.text: Use [lem-coef-infinity-monomorphism-boundary-cells] for $\varnothing\hookrightarrow N(I)$: the next skeleton is obtained by adjoining one $\Delta^n$ for every nondegenerate $n$-simplex $\sigma$ along its boundary, for $n\geq1$. Pull this pushout back along $N\pi$ and adjoin $A$. This preserves the degreewise pushout: in a given degree each new element has a base element outside the previous skeleton, hence a unique summand; pairs with the same base element are identified precisely when their base representatives are identified. Write $X_\sigma=N(P)\times_{N(I)}\Delta^n$ and $A_\sigma=A\times_{N(I)}\Delta^n$. The attaching subset is $B_\sigma=A_\sigma\cup(X_\sigma\times_{\Delta^n}\partial\Delta^n)$. We obtain the pushout adjoining all $X_\sigma$ to $S_{n-1}$ along all $B_\sigma$. The maps $X_\sigma\to N(P)$ need not be injective; the pushout argument uses the degreewise attaching description, so it includes repeated base vertices and nontrivial endomorphisms in $I$.

source.place: Lemma 7.3.4.5, proof opening reduction to a simplex and its boundary; explicit degreewise skeletal assembly

proof.text: Assume a map $F_{n-1}:S_{n-1}\to\mathcal E$ extending $F_0$ has been constructed. A base simplex $\sigma$ is a functor $[n]\to I$. Nerves commute with strict pullbacks directly from their definition by functors $[q]\to(-)$, so $X_\sigma$ is the nerve of the strict pullback $[n]\times_I P$. This category identifies with $P_{U\sigma}$ of [lem-coef-infinity-fiber-cocone-simplex-extension]: an object over $r$ is either $(r,x)$, $x\in U(\sigma(r))$, or the second-copy vertex $r$; arrows over $r\leq s$ have exactly the fiber component and mixed rule in that node. Its $K$ part is $A_\sigma$ and its boundary subset is exactly $B_\sigma$. All vertices of $\Delta^n$ lie in its boundary since $n\geq1$, and the corresponding restricted cocones are the already fixed $c_{\sigma(r)}$, which are colimiting by Step 1. Apply that node to the map on $B_\sigma$ induced by $F_{n-1}$. It gives a lift on $X_\sigma$ agreeing exactly on $B_\sigma$. Choose such a lift for each of the small set of nondegenerate $n$-simplices. The pushout in Step 3 glues these maps to $F_n:S_n\to\mathcal E$, and its restriction is exactly $F_{n-1}$.

source.place: Lemma 7.3.4.5, local extension, used at each skeletal attachment

proof.text: Continue this induction for every positive integer $n$. Every simplex of $N(I)$ lies in some skeleton by the exhaustive cell presentation in Step 3; therefore every simplex of $N(P)$ lies in some $S_n$. For a simplex $s$ of $N(P)$ set $\overline Q(s)=F_n(s)$ for any $n$ with $s\in S_n$. This is independent of $n$ because consecutive maps agree on the entire preceding subset. Every face and degeneracy of $s$ lies in the same simplicial subset, where $F_n$ respects that operator. Hence this rule is a simplicial map on $N(P)$, restricting exactly to $Q$ on $A$. It retains every $c_i$, since no extension changes $S_0$. Thus the specified arrows $(i,x)\to i$ induce the same colimiting coherent cocones as in Step 1. No colimits in $\mathcal E$ other than the assumed fiber colimits have been taken. If $I$ is empty, both $K$ and $P$ are empty and the original empty map is the required extension.

source.place: Lemma 7.3.4.6, conclusion; compatible union and verification of every prescribed fiber cocone

proof_origin.place: Proof paragraph 2, coherent tower enhancement foundation; skeletal expansion of the local-to-global assembly in Kerodon 7.3.4.5--7.3.4.7. Online sources read; WANTED archived versions.
